newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong Oil starts gasoline exports.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong Oil starts gasoline exports.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Oil Refining Co, an affiliate of Ssangyong Group, has signed its first gasoline export deals this month after the start-up of its new facility, company officials said on Wednesday.
The officials said no plans were set on how much Ssangyong plans to export in May.
"With annual maintenance shutdown scheduled for next month, it's hard to say how much would be available for export," one official said.
Ssangyong plans to close down its 150,000 bpd crude distillation unit between May 6 and June 1. The company has a total refining capacity of 443,000 bpd.
Ssangyong Oil's new 40,000 barrels-per-day residue fluid catalytic cracker (RFCC), started operations earlier this month and is scheduled for full production in late April.
"Two gasoline cargoes were sold for the first time," one Ssangyong official said.
The officials said one gasoline cargo was sold to U.S. refiner Coastal. The cargo will be delivered to Coastal's storage facility in the Philippines.
The other cargo was purchased by European major British Petroleum in Singapore. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5643
